title: Double Smash Burgers
subtitle: Crispy edges, melty cheese, crew-approved
description: Crispy edges, melty cheese, crew-approved. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Make the dirty sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, relish, Worcestershire, garlic powder, and smoked paprika until creamy and pink-tan. Dirty sauce should taste tangy-savory-sweet — not plain mayo. Hold refrigerated until service; room-temp sauce on hot burgers is fine, but don't water it down.

steps.title: Caramelize the onions
steps.instruction: Slice onions into thin half-moons. Melt butter in a wide pan over medium-low — gentle heat is the secret (high heat burns before sweet). Stir every 3–4 minutes until onions turn jammy, mahogany, and smell like candy (25–30 min). They should melt when pressed, not hold crunch. Season lightly with salt. Common mistake: rushing — pale onions taste sharp, not diner-sweet.

steps.title: Prep and portion the beef
steps.instruction: Divide beef into 3 oz loose balls — about twenty, enough for eight double stacks plus seconds. Do not pack tight; air pockets help the smash spread. Chill until smash time if the kitchen is warm; cold fat renders into crispy edges. Shred iceberg fine; drain pickle chips on paper towels so buns don't sog.

steps.title: Toast the potato buns
steps.instruction: Butter cut sides of potato buns generously. Toast on griddle or skillet until edges are golden and centers still soft — you want a glossy, buttery shell that won't dissolve under sauce. Toast just before smashing so buns stay warm. Stack cut-side up on a sheet pan.

steps.title: Smash the first patty
steps.instruction: Heat cast iron or flat griddle until a water droplet dances and evaporates in 2 seconds — that's smash heat. Film lightly with the neutral high-heat oil. Place a beef ball, immediately smash flat with a stiff spatula (use parchment on spatula if it sticks). Press 10 seconds so meat spreads thin with lacy edges creeping past the ball. Season with salt and pepper. Don't move — crust is forming. Cook until edges look deep brown and lacey, top still pink-red, about 90 seconds.

steps.title: Flip, cheese, stack the second patty
steps.instruction: Scrape and flip with confidence — the crust should release cleanly. Lay American cheese on the cooked side immediately; residual heat melts cheese in 30–45 seconds (cheese should drape, not sit solid). Add a fresh beef ball on the cheese, smash again, season, and cook second crust 90 seconds. Flip once more, add second cheese slice, and stack both patties cheese-side-in so you get a molten core. Timing matters: cheese goes on the hot face right after flip, not before — otherwise it oils out.

steps.title: Optional bacon on the side
steps.instruction: Lay bacon in cold pan, turn to medium, cook until shatter-crisp. Blot on towels — wet bacon steams the bun. Hold warm; add only at assembly so it stays crisp.

steps.title: Bake the diner fries at 425°F
steps.instruction: Spread fries in a single layer — crowded pans steam instead of crisp. Bake until deeply golden with audible crunch when shaken. Season with salt immediately out of the oven (hot fat grabs seasoning). Hold in warm oven with door cracked.

steps.title: Build the stacks in order
steps.instruction: Bottom bun → dirty sauce → shredded lettuce (barrier against juice) → pickles → double stack (cheese melted between patties) → spoon of caramelized onions → optional bacon → more dirty sauce on top bun → crown. Press lightly so stack sets. Serve within 2 minutes — smash burgers lose their crisp edge fast. Crew eats open-faced at the line if stacks are tall.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: Smash burgers don't hold — the crisp edge dies in minutes. If tones drop mid-cook, kill the griddle and stop smashing; hold cooked patties uncovered on a rack in a 200°F oven at 140°F or above (never below 140°F past 30 minutes) and keep raw beef balls cold. On return, re-crisp patties on the hot griddle 30 seconds a side and build to order — never sauce a bun that's been sitting.

steps.title: Hold finished stacks for the line
steps.instruction: Keep completed double stacks on a wire rack in a 200°F oven up to 8 minutes — never stack hot burgers or bottoms steam soggy. Wipe the griddle between batches so burnt fat does not taint the next round. Fries hold in a warm pan with the door cracked.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool cooked patties and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Smash once, hard, in the first 10 seconds — once the crust forms, re-smashing tears the lacy edge off.
American cheese melts faster and smoother than cheddar; use it for that diner drape.
Dirty sauce on both bun faces, and put the shredded lettuce between sauce and patty as a juice barrier so the bottom bun survives.
Wipe the griddle between batches — burnt fat from the last round turns the next patties bitter.
Season the patty right after you smash it, on the raw face, so the salt sets into the crust instead of sitting on top.
tonightSpread: Main: Double smash burgers with caramelized onions
Sides: diner fries, dill pickle chips
Condiments: dirty sauce, shredded iceberg, optional bacon
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool cooked patties in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Store buns separately — stacked overnight turns crisp edges soft.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Crispy edges, melty cheese, crew-approved. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free bun/bread and toast on a separate, clean surface. Use a certified gluten-free Worcestershire sauce. Use a certified gluten-free frozen fry/tot brand, or fresh-cut potatoes.

adaptable.label: Dairy-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a dairy-free cheese shred/block alternative. Use a plant-based butter/margarine.
